name: _badblocks_set
prose: Precondition: bb points to an initialized struct badblocks whose page table is valid; the caller must not hold bb->lock (the function takes the write seqlock itself with interrupts saved); s and sectors give the range and acknowledged says whether new entries are acknowledged. Postcondition: returns false, without taking the lock or changing anything, if bb->shift < 0 (badblocks disabled) or sectors == 0. Otherwise (note the rounddown/roundup calls under bb->shift are statement expressions whose results are discarded, so s and sectors are NOT rounded) it takes the write seqlock and repeatedly inserts, merges, combines or overwrites entries for [s, s+sectors), advancing s and shrinking sectors by the length handled each pass (a pass may also skip over a range that is already recorded with ack state that cannot be overwritten). It stops early, with only part of the range (possibly none) recorded, when the table is full or when a front overwrite would need extra table slots (extra > 0) that cannot be had; it then returns false. If the whole range is processed it also tries to combine with the following entry (try_adjacent_combine) and returns true. The return value is exactly (remaining sectors == 0). If at least one entry was added or merged (added != 0) it calls set_changed(bb) and, if acknowledged is 0, sets bb->unacked_exist = 1, else calls badblocks_update_acked(bb). bb->count is updated for every insertion, combine or overwrite. The write seqlock is released (interrupt flags restored) on every path that took it.
note: Real function name is _badblocks_set; slice contains the whole function. Prose rewritten: false also when table full or front-overwrite needs extra slots; rounding is a no-op in this source.

name: BFQ_BFQQ_FNS(just_created)
prose: Generated function bfq_mark_bfqq_just_created(bfqq). Precondition: bfqq points to a valid struct bfq_queue. Postcondition: sets bit BFQQF_just_created in bfqq->flags using the non-atomic __set_bit (the caller must serialise flag updates, e.g. by holding the bfq_data lock); returns nothing; no lock, reference or memory is acquired or released.
note: Macro-generated function: the real name does not occur literally in the source, so the name field is the exact macro invocation that generates it (BFQ_BFQQ_FNS defines bfq_mark_bfqq_X, bfq_clear_bfqq_X and bfq_bfqq_X).

name: BFQ_BFQQ_FNS(just_created)
prose: Generated function bfq_clear_bfqq_just_created(bfqq). Precondition: bfqq points to a valid struct bfq_queue. Postcondition: clears bit BFQQF_just_created in bfqq->flags using the non-atomic __clear_bit (the caller must serialise flag updates); returns nothing; no lock, reference or memory is acquired or released.
note: Macro-generated function: the real name does not occur literally in the source, so the name field is the exact macro invocation that generates it (BFQ_BFQQ_FNS defines bfq_mark_bfqq_X, bfq_clear_bfqq_X and bfq_bfqq_X).

name: BFQ_BFQQ_FNS(just_created)
prose: Generated function bfq_bfqq_just_created(bfqq). Precondition: bfqq points to a valid struct bfq_queue. Postcondition: returns the result of test_bit(BFQQF_just_created, &bfqq->flags), i.e. nonzero (1) if that bit is set and 0 if it is clear; bfqq->flags is not modified and no lock, reference or memory is acquired or released.
note: Macro-generated function: the real name does not occur literally in the source, so the name field is the exact macro invocation that generates it (BFQ_BFQQ_FNS defines bfq_mark_bfqq_X, bfq_clear_bfqq_X and bfq_bfqq_X).

name: bfq_bfqq_resume_state
prose: Precondition: bfqq, bfqd and bic are valid, bic->bfqq_data[bfqq->actuator_idx] holds the state previously saved for bfqq, the caller holds the bfq_data lock, and bfq_already_existing says whether bfqq was already in use. Postcondition: the function returns nothing. It first records busy = bfq_already_existing && bfq_bfqq_busy(bfqq) and old_wr_coeff = 1. It then copies the saved values into bfqq: the has_short_ttime and IO_bound flags are marked or cleared according to the saved flags, and last_serv_time_ns, inject_limit, decrease_time_jif, entity.new_weight (from saved_weight), ttime, io_start_time, tot_idle_time, service_from_wr, wr_start_at_switch_to_srt, last_wr_start_finish and wr_cur_max_time are overwritten. wr_coeff is overwritten with saved_wr_coeff only if bfqd->low_latency is set, in which case old_wr_coeff becomes the previous wr_coeff; otherwise wr_coeff and old_wr_coeff (still 1) are left as they were. Then, if bfqq->wr_coeff > 1 and (bfqq is in a large burst or last_wr_start_finish + wr_cur_max_time is already in the past): if wr_cur_max_time == bfqd->bfq_wr_rt_max_time and bfqq is not in a large burst and wr_start_at_switch_to_srt + bfq_wr_duration(bfqd) is not before the current time, weight raising is switched back to interactive (wr_coeff = bfqd->bfq_wr_coeff, wr_cur_max_time = bfq_wr_duration(bfqd), last_wr_start_finish = wr_start_at_switch_to_srt); otherwise wr_coeff is set to 1. In all cases entity.prio_changed is set to 1. If busy is false the function then returns; if busy is true, bfqd->wr_busy_queues is incremented when old_wr_coeff == 1 and the final wr_coeff > 1, decremented when old_wr_coeff > 1 and the final wr_coeff == 1, and unchanged otherwise. No lock is taken or released and no reference or memory is acquired or released.

name: bfq_bfqq_save_state
prose: Precondition: bfqq points to a valid struct bfq_queue and the caller holds the bfq_data lock. Postcondition: the function returns nothing. If bfqq->bic is NULL it returns immediately without storing anything (the per-actuator slot address &bic->bfqq_data[a_idx] is computed first but never dereferenced when bic is NULL). Otherwise it stores into bic->bfqq_data[bfqq->actuator_idx]: saved_last_serv_time_ns, saved_inject_limit, saved_decrease_time_jif, saved_weight (from entity.orig_weight), saved_ttime, saved_has_short_ttime, saved_IO_bound, saved_io_start_time, saved_tot_idle_time, saved_in_large_burst, and was_in_burst_list (true iff bfqq->burst_list_node is hashed). Then, if bfqq is just created and not in a large burst and bfqq->bfqd->low_latency is set, it stores the weight-raising state bfqq would have deserved: saved_wr_coeff = bfqd->bfq_wr_coeff, saved_wr_start_at_switch_to_srt = bfq_smallest_from_now(), saved_wr_cur_max_time = bfq_wr_duration(bfqd), saved_last_wr_start_finish = jiffies, and leaves saved_service_from_wr unchanged; otherwise it stores bfqq->wr_coeff, wr_start_at_switch_to_srt, service_from_wr, last_wr_start_finish and wr_cur_max_time. bfqq itself is not modified and no lock, reference or memory is acquired or released.

name: __bfq_bfqq_expire
prose: Precondition: bfqd is the bfq_data whose in-service queue is bfqq (the queue being expired), reason is the expiration cause, and the caller holds the bfq_data lock. Postcondition: if bfqq is cooperative (bfq_bfqq_coop) and BFQQ_SEEKY(bfqq) holds, bfqq is marked split_coop. Then, if bfqq->sort_list is empty and it is not the case that (reason == BFQQE_PREEMPTED and idling is needed for service guarantees), then bfqq->budget_timeout is set to jiffies only if bfqq->dispatched == 0, and bfqq is removed from the busy queues with bfq_del_bfqq_busy(bfqq, true); otherwise bfqq is requeued with bfq_requeue_bfqq(bfqd, bfqq, true) and, if !bfqd->nonrot_with_queueing and bfqq->sort_list is non-empty, bfq_pos_tree_add_move(bfqd, bfqq) re-sorts it in the position tree. Finally it returns the value of __bfq_bfqd_reset_in_service(bfqd), which clears the in-service entities of bfqd and returns true iff that caused bfqq to be freed (so the caller must not touch bfqq when true), false otherwise. The function does not itself return a constant true.

name: bfq_bfqq_expire
prose: Precondition: bfqd is the bfq_data whose in-service queue is bfqq, compensate says whether to compensate for idle-time overestimation, reason is a valid expiration cause, and the caller holds the bfq_data lock. Postcondition: the function returns nothing. It computes slow and delta (delta is the time in milliseconds for which the queue was served, as set by bfq_bfqq_is_slow) with bfq_bfqq_is_slow. If bfqq->wr_coeff == 1 and (slow, or reason == BFQQE_BUDGET_TIMEOUT with budget left >= entity->budget / 3), the queue is charged delta (time) instead of service via bfq_bfqq_charge_time. If bfqd->low_latency and wr_coeff == 1, last_wr_start_finish is set to jiffies. If bfqd->low_latency, bfqd->bfq_wr_max_softrt_rate > 0 and bfqq->sort_list is empty: soft_rt_next_start is recomputed with bfq_bfqq_softrt_next_start when bfqq->dispatched == 0, else if dispatched > 0 the softrt_update flag is marked. bfqd->rqs_injected and bfqd->wait_dispatch are set to false and bfqd->waited_rq to NULL. The budget is recomputed with __bfq_bfqq_recalc_budget(bfqd, bfqq, reason) and the queue expired with __bfq_bfqq_expire; if that returns true (bfqq freed) the function returns at once. Otherwise: if bfqq is not busy and reason is neither BFQQE_BUDGET_TIMEOUT nor BFQQE_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED the queue is marked non_blocking_wait_rq and its entity->service is kept, else entity->service is set to 0; in both cases the service counter of every ancestor (parent) entity is then reset to 0. No lock or reference is acquired or released.

name: bfq_set_next_ioprio_data
prose: Precondition: bfqq and bic are valid; the caller serialises access to bfqq. Postcondition: the function returns nothing. If bfqq->bfqd is NULL it returns immediately and modifies nothing. Otherwise, with ioprio_class = IOPRIO_PRIO_CLASS(bic->ioprio): for IOPRIO_CLASS_RT or IOPRIO_CLASS_BE, new_ioprio = IOPRIO_PRIO_LEVEL(bic->ioprio) and new_ioprio_class is that class; for IOPRIO_CLASS_IDLE, new_ioprio_class = IOPRIO_CLASS_IDLE and new_ioprio = IOPRIO_NR_LEVELS - 1; for IOPRIO_CLASS_NONE, and for any unrecognised class (which also logs an error), new_ioprio = task_nice_ioprio(current) and new_ioprio_class = task_nice_ioclass(current). If the resulting new_ioprio is >= IOPRIO_NR_LEVELS a critical message is logged and it is clamped to IOPRIO_NR_LEVELS - 1. Finally entity.new_weight = bfq_ioprio_to_weight(new_ioprio) and entity.prio_changed = 1. No lock or reference is acquired or released.

name: bfq_update_has_short_ttime
prose: Precondition: bfqd, bfqq and bic are valid, bic->icq.ioc is valid, and the caller holds the bfq_data lock. Postcondition: the function returns nothing. It returns without changing any state if bfqq is not sync, or bfqq is in the idle I/O class, or bfqd->bfq_slice_idle == 0, or bfqq->split_time + bfqd->bfq_wr_min_idle_time is not before the current time (time_is_after_eq_jiffies, i.e. bfqq was split too recently). Otherwise has_short_ttime is computed as false if atomic_read(&bic->icq.ioc->active_ref) == 0 or (the think-time sample count is valid and bfqq->ttime.ttime_mean > bfqd->bfq_slice_idle / 2), and true otherwise; the has_short_ttime flag of bfqq is marked when true and cleared when false. If the value of the flag changed, bfqq->last_serv_time_ns == 0, and (bfqq->decrease_time_jif + 100 ms is not after the current time, or the new value is false), then bfq_reset_inject_limit(bfqd, bfqq) is called. No lock or reference is acquired or released.

name: blk_next_bio
prose: Precondition: bdev, nr_pages, opf and gfp are valid arguments for bio_alloc; bio is either NULL or a bio ready to be submitted whose bi_private and bi_end_io are both unset (bio_chain BUG_ONs otherwise); if bio is non-NULL the allocation must not fail (gfp must include __GFP_DIRECT_RECLAIM), because bio_alloc returning NULL would make bio_chain dereference a NULL parent. Postcondition: returns the newly allocated bio (bio_alloc(bdev, nr_pages, opf, gfp)), which is NULL only if bio is NULL and the allocation failed. If bio is non-NULL it is chained to the new bio (bio->bi_private = new bio, bio->bi_end_io = bio_chain_endio, the remaining count of the new bio incremented) and then submitted with submit_bio, so ownership of bio passes to the block layer and the caller must not use it afterwards; if bio is NULL nothing is chained or submitted. The caller owns the returned bio.

name: bio_alloc_rescue
prose: Precondition: work is the rescue_work member of an initialized struct bio_set whose rescue_lock and rescue_list are valid. Postcondition: the function returns nothing. It loops: under bs->rescue_lock it pops one bio from bs->rescue_list (bio_list_pop), releases the lock, and if the bio is non-NULL submits it with submit_bio_noacct (without holding the lock) and repeats; it returns when a pop under the lock yields NULL, i.e. when the list was found empty at that check (other contexts may add bios afterwards). Every bio popped is submitted exactly once; the spinlock is released on every iteration and on return.

name: blkcg_activate_policy
prose: Precondition: disk is a valid gendisk with a request queue, pol is a registered blkcg_policy, the caller may sleep (it can freeze the queue, takes q->blkcg_mutex and q->queue_lock, and allocates with GFP_KERNEL), and activation and deactivation of policies on the queue are serialised by the caller. Postcondition: if the policy is already enabled on the queue (blkcg_policy_enabled) it returns 0 immediately without changing anything. Otherwise, if pol->pd_alloc_fn or pol->pd_free_fn is NULL it emits WARN_ON_ONCE and returns -EINVAL without changing anything. Otherwise it freezes the queue if it is blk-mq, takes q->blkcg_mutex, and walks q->blkg_list in reverse under q->queue_lock, allocating (GFP_NOWAIT, falling back to a GFP_KERNEL preallocation after dropping the lock, pinning the blkg meanwhile, and retrying) a policy data for each blkg that has no pd for pol and is still linked in its blkcg; each new pd is linked to the blkg, initialised (pd_init_fn, if any), onlined (pd_online_fn, if any) and marked online under blkcg->lock. On success it sets the pol->plid bit in q->blkcg_pols and returns 0. If the GFP_KERNEL preallocation fails, it offlines (pd_offline_fn if online) and frees (pd_free_fn) every pd of this policy found on q->blkg_list, clears the blkg->pd slots, leaves the plid bit clear and returns -ENOMEM. On every path after the checks it releases q->blkcg_mutex, unfreezes the queue if it was frozen, drops the reference on any pinned blkg and frees any unused preallocated pd.

name: blkg_create
prose: Precondition: disk->queue->queue_lock is held by the caller (lockdep asserted) and stays held; blkcg is a valid blkcg; new_blkg is NULL or a blkg obtained from blkg_alloc for this blkcg and disk. The function always consumes new_blkg: the caller must not use or free it afterwards. Postcondition: on success it returns the blkg (new_blkg, or a freshly allocated one with GFP_NOWAIT) after: calling pd_init_fn on its pds, inserting it into blkcg->blkg_tree (keyed by the queue id), at the head of blkcg->blkg_list and of the queue blkg_list, calling pd_online_fn on each pd and setting online on the pds and the blkg; it holds a css reference on blkcg taken by css_tryget_online and, if blkcg has a parent, a reference on the parent blkg (blkg->parent), and the blkg keeps the queue reference taken by blkg_alloc. On failure it returns ERR_PTR(-ENODEV) if the queue is dying (css not taken), if css_tryget_online fails (css not taken), or if blkcg has a parent but no parent blkg is found (WARN_ON_ONCE, css reference dropped with css_put), ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM) if new_blkg was NULL and the GFP_NOWAIT allocation fails (css reference dropped), or ERR_PTR of the radix_tree_insert error. In the -ENODEV, parent-lookup and allocation-failure paths a non-NULL new_blkg is released with blkg_free (an asynchronous work item that frees its pds and queue reference). In the radix_tree_insert failure case the blkg is not linked anywhere or marked online and percpu_ref_kill(&blkg->refcnt) is called, so blkg_release later drops the css and parent-blkg references and frees it.

name: errno_to_blk_status
prose: Precondition: none; errno may be any int. Postcondition: the function returns the blk_status_t whose value is the index of the first entry of the designated-initialiser table blk_errors whose errno field equals the argument, and BLK_STS_IOERR (10) when no entry matches. The mapping is: 0 -> 0 (BLK_STS_OK), -EOPNOTSUPP -> 1, -ETIMEDOUT -> 2, -ENOSPC -> 3, -ENOLINK -> 4, -EREMOTEIO -> 5, -EBADE -> 6, -ENODATA -> 7, -EILSEQ -> 8, -ENOMEM -> 9, -EIO -> 10, -EREMCHG -> 11, -EAGAIN -> 12, -EBUSY -> 13, -ETOOMANYREFS -> 14, -EOVERFLOW -> 15, -ENODEV -> 16, -ETIME -> 17, -EINVAL -> 19 (index 18 of the table is unused and holds errno 0, so it is never selected because index 0 matches first), and every other value -> 10. It has no side effects and acquires or releases no lock, reference or memory.
contract: /*@ requires \true; ensures (errno == 0 ? result == 0 : errno == -95 ? result == 1 : errno == -110 ? result == 2 : errno == -28 ? result == 3 : errno == -67 ? result == 4 : errno == -121 ? result == 5 : errno == -52 ? result == 6 : errno == -61 ? result == 7 : errno == -84 ? result == 8 : errno == -12 ? result == 9 : errno == -5 ? result == 10 : errno == -78 ? result == 11 : errno == -11 ? result == 12 : errno == -16 ? result == 13 : errno == -109 ? result == 14 : errno == -75 ? result == 15 : errno == -19 ? result == 16 : errno == -62 ? result == 17 : errno == -22 ? result == 19 : result == 10) && (result != 0 || errno == 0); */
note: Previous prose/contract wrongly assumed table index = row order (EBADE as -1, EBUSY 10, ENODEV 12, EINVAL 17, IOERR 18). Table is indexed by BLK_STS_* values; values taken from include/linux/blk_types.h and generic x86 errno numbers.

name: blk_crypto_get_keyslot
prose: Precondition: profile is a valid initialised blk_crypto_profile, key is a valid key supported by it, slot_ptr is a valid pointer, and the caller may sleep (the function can wait for an idle slot and calls the driver keyslot_program op). Postcondition: *slot_ptr is first set to NULL. If profile->num_slots == 0 it returns BLK_STS_OK with *slot_ptr left NULL (no keyslot is needed). Otherwise it looks for a slot already holding key under the read lock and, if found, grabs a reference on it (slot_refs incremented, slot removed from the idle LRU list if the count went 0 to 1), stores it in *slot_ptr and returns BLK_STS_OK. If not found it enters hw-exclusive mode (pm_runtime_get_sync if profile->dev, plus the write lock), re-checks for a slot holding key (same success result), and otherwise waits, sleeping, until profile->idle_slots is non-empty, then takes the first idle slot, programs key into it with ll_ops.keyslot_program. If programming fails it wakes the idle-slot waiters, leaves hw-exclusive mode and returns errno_to_blk_status(err) with *slot_ptr still NULL and no reference held. If programming succeeds, the slot is unhashed from its old key (if it had one), assigned key, hashed under key, given slot_refs = 1 and removed from the idle LRU list; it is stored in *slot_ptr and BLK_STS_OK is returned. On success with a slot the caller owns one reference and must release it with blk_crypto_put_keyslot. The profile lock and runtime-PM reference taken for hw-exclusive mode are released on every path.
note: Previously dropped as not a function (slice cut the head); it is a real function.

name: iocg_activate
prose: Precondition: iocg is a valid ioc_gq with valid iocg->ioc, now points to a writable struct ioc_now, the caller does not hold ioc->lock and may disable interrupts (the function takes ioc->lock with spin_lock_irq and releases it before returning on every path that took it). Postcondition: returns true if iocg is (or after this call becomes) active, false otherwise. If iocg->active_list is already non-empty it refreshes *now with ioc_now, sets iocg->active_period to the current ioc->cur_period if it differs, and returns true without taking the lock. Else if iocg->child_active_sum is non-zero it returns false immediately without changing anything (including *now). Otherwise it takes ioc->lock, refreshes *now, sets iocg->active_period to cur_period, and: if iocg is already on the active list returns true; if any ancestor iocg at levels level-1 down to 1 is on the active list, or child_active_sum is non-zero, returns false (active_period has already been updated); else it shifts iocg->vtime and iocg->done_vtime so that vtime equals now->vnow - ioc->margins.target, invalidates the cached hweight (hweight_gen = ioc->hweight_gen - 1), adds iocg to ioc->active_iocgs, calls propagate_weights with iocg->weight and last_inuse (or weight if last_inuse is 0), records iocg->activated_at = now->now, and if ioc->running was IOC_IDLE sets it to IOC_RUNNING, sets dfgv_period_at = now->now, dfgv_period_rem = 0 and starts a period with ioc_start_period; then returns true.
note: Previously dropped; real function, previous prose claimed it always returns true.

name: blkiolatency_timer_fn
prose: Precondition: t is the timer field of an initialised struct blk_iolatency whose rqos.disk, its queue and root_blkg are valid; runs in timer (softirq) context. Postcondition: returns nothing. Under rcu_read_lock it visits the root blkg and every descendant (pre-order). For each blkg on which blkg_tryget succeeds (others are skipped) and which has an iolatency group whose child_lat scale_cookie is below DEFAULT_SCALE_COOKIE, it takes lat_info->lock with interrupts saved and then: does nothing if last_scale_event >= now (now is the time sampled at entry); otherwise, if scale_grp is NULL, it calls scale_cookie_change(iolat->blkiolat, lat_info, true) to scale the cookie up; otherwise, if now - last_scale_event >= 5 seconds, it sets scale_grp to NULL; otherwise it changes nothing. The lock is released and the blkg reference dropped with blkg_put for every blkg whose reference was obtained, and the RCU read lock is released before return.

name: blk_mq_num_possible_queues
prose: Precondition: none (reads cpu_possible_mask, which is stable after boot). Postcondition: returns min_not_zero(N, max_queues) where N is the number of CPUs in cpu_possible_mask: if N and max_queues are both non-zero the result is the smaller; if max_queues is 0 the result is N; if N is 0 the result is max_queues. It has no side effects and acquires or releases no lock, reference or memory.

name: blk_mq_num_online_queues
prose: Precondition: none (reads cpu_online_mask, which may change concurrently with CPU hotplug, so the result is a snapshot). Postcondition: returns min_not_zero(N, max_queues) where N is the number of CPUs in cpu_online_mask: if N and max_queues are both non-zero the result is the smaller; if max_queues is 0 the result is N; if N is 0 the result is max_queues. It has no side effects and acquires or releases no lock, reference or memory.

name: blk_mq_is_sync_read
prose: Precondition: none; opf may be any blk_opf_t (32-bit) value. Postcondition: returns true iff op_is_sync(opf) holds and op_is_write(opf) does not. op_is_sync(opf) is true when the operation code (opf & 0xff) is REQ_OP_READ (0) or any of the flags REQ_SYNC (0x800), REQ_FUA (0x20000) or REQ_PREFLUSH (0x40000) is set in opf; op_is_write(opf) is true when bit 0 of opf is set. So the result is ((opf & 0xff) == 0 || (opf & 0x60800) != 0) && (opf & 1) == 0. It has no side effects and acquires or releases no lock, reference or memory.
note: Previous version omitted REQ_FUA and REQ_PREFLUSH from op_is_sync (checked in include/linux/blk_types.h).

name: blk_mq_hctx_next_cpu
prose: Precondition: hctx is a valid hardware context with valid hctx->queue, cpumask, next_cpu and next_cpu_batch; the caller serialises updates of next_cpu/next_cpu_batch (they are not atomic). Postcondition: returns WORK_CPU_UNBOUND, without changing hctx, if the queue has exactly one hardware queue or hctx->next_cpu >= nr_cpu_ids (empty cpumask). Otherwise it decrements hctx->next_cpu_batch; if the result is <= 0 it selects the next CPU after hctx->next_cpu that is in both hctx->cpumask and cpu_online_mask, wrapping to blk_mq_first_mapped_cpu(hctx) (first online CPU of the mask, or its first CPU even if offline when none is online), and resets next_cpu_batch to BLK_MQ_CPU_WORK_BATCH (8). If the candidate CPU is not online it tries the selection once more; if the candidate is still offline it stores it in hctx->next_cpu, sets hctx->next_cpu_batch = 1 and returns WORK_CPU_UNBOUND. Otherwise it stores the online candidate in hctx->next_cpu and returns it. So a CPU number returned is always an online CPU.

name: blk_post_runtime_suspend
prose: Precondition: q is a valid request queue, blk_pre_runtime_suspend was called for this suspend attempt, and err is the result of the driver runtime_suspend callback; the caller does not hold q->queue_lock. Postcondition: returns nothing. If q->dev is NULL it returns immediately and changes nothing. Otherwise under q->queue_lock (irq-disabling) it sets q->rpm_status = RPM_SUSPENDED when err == 0; when err != 0 it sets q->rpm_status = RPM_ACTIVE and calls pm_runtime_mark_last_busy(q->dev). After the lock is released, if err != 0 it calls blk_clear_pm_only(q), which decrements q->pm_only and, when it reaches 0, wakes waiters on q->mq_freeze_wq. When err == 0 pm_only is left unchanged.

name: blk_timeout_init
prose: Precondition: none; runs once as an initcall. Postcondition: sets the file-static blk_timeout_mask to roundup_pow_of_two(HZ) - 1 and returns 0 always. No lock, reference or memory is acquired or released.

name: blk_rq_timeout
prose: Precondition: timeout is a jiffies-based expiry value; blk_timeout_mask has been set by blk_timeout_init. Postcondition: with maxt = blk_round_jiffies(jiffies + BLK_MAX_TIMEOUT), where BLK_MAX_TIMEOUT is 5 * HZ and blk_round_jiffies(j) = j + blk_timeout_mask + 1, the function returns maxt if time_after(timeout, maxt) (wrap-safe comparison: timeout is later than maxt), and returns timeout unchanged otherwise. So the result never lies after maxt and is never later than timeout. No side effects; no lock, reference or memory is acquired or released.

name: blk_add_timer
prose: Precondition: req points to a request about to start, req->q is a valid request queue; the caller may be in any context (the timer is modified with mod_timer). Postcondition: returns nothing. If req->timeout was 0 it is set to q->rq_timeout. RQF_TIMED_OUT is cleared in req->rq_flags. req->deadline is set (WRITE_ONCE) to jiffies + req->timeout (unrounded). Let expiry = blk_rq_timeout(blk_round_jiffies(jiffies + req->timeout)) (computed from the same jiffies sample). The queue timer q->timeout is re-armed with mod_timer(&q->timeout, expiry) if and only if either the timer is not pending, or expiry is before q->timeout.expires and q->timeout.expires - expiry >= HZ / 2. In every other case (timer pending and expiry not earlier, or earlier by less than HZ/2) the timer is left unchanged, so the timer may fire later than expiry by up to HZ/2 - 1 jiffies. No lock, reference or memory is acquired or released.

name: __disk_unblock_events
prose: Precondition: disk is valid with disk->ev non-NULL; the caller does not hold ev->lock; the caller holds a block count taken by disk_block_events. Postcondition: returns nothing. Under ev->lock (irq state saved): if ev->block <= 0 it emits WARN_ON_ONCE and changes nothing; otherwise it decrements ev->block; if the result is still non-zero nothing else happens; if it reaches zero it computes intv = disk_events_poll_jiffies(disk) and, if check_now is true, queues ev->dwork on system_freezable_power_efficient_wq with delay 0, else if intv != 0 queues it with delay intv, else (check_now false and intv == 0) queues nothing. The lock is released on every path.

name: disk_flush_events
prose: Precondition: disk is a valid gendisk (disk->ev may be NULL); the caller does not hold ev->lock. Postcondition: returns nothing. If disk->ev is NULL it returns at once and changes nothing. Otherwise, under ev->lock (irq-disabling), mask is ORed into ev->clearing, and if ev->block is 0 the delayed work ev->dwork on system_freezable_power_efficient_wq is rescheduled with delay 0 via mod_delayed_work (replacing any pending timer); if ev->block is non-zero no work is scheduled. The lock is released before return.

name: disk_event_uevent
prose: Precondition: disk is a valid gendisk and events is a bitmask of DISK_EVENT_* bits. Postcondition: returns nothing. It builds an environment list containing, for each index i of the disk_uevents table ("DISK_MEDIA_CHANGE=1", "DISK_EJECT_REQUEST=1") for which bit (1 << i) is set in both events and disk->events, that string, in table order. If at least one string was added it emits a KOBJ_CHANGE uevent on the disk kobject with that environment (kobject_uevent_env); if none matched no uevent is sent. It does not check DISK_EVENT_FLAG_UEVENT (that is done by the caller disk_check_events), takes no lock itself and holds no reference after return.

name: disk_clear_events
prose: Precondition: the caller may sleep (it blocks and cancels event work synchronously and calls the driver check_events op); disk is valid and disk->ev may be NULL. Postcondition: if disk->ev is NULL it returns 0 with no other effect. Otherwise it calls disk_block_events (incrementing ev->block, and on the first block cancelling the event work synchronously); then, under ev->lock, sets clearing = mask | ev->clearing and ev->clearing = 0; runs disk_check_events, which calls the driver check_events(disk, clearing), ORs the newly reported events not already pending into ev->pending, increments the disk sequence number on a media-change event and emits uevents if DISK_EVENT_FLAG_UEVENT is set; calls __disk_unblock_events(disk, ev->clearing != 0) (decrementing ev->block and, when it reaches zero, queueing the event work immediately if ev->clearing is non-zero or after the poll interval if that is non-zero); and finally, under ev->lock, returns ev->pending & mask while clearing exactly those mask bits from ev->pending. ev->block is the same on return as on entry (other events bits in pending outside mask are kept).

name: elevator_switch
prose: Precondition: the caller holds q->elevator_lock and q->mq_freeze_depth is non-zero (the queue is frozen); ctx is a valid elv_change_ctx with ctx->name a string and ctx->res prepared by the caller. Postcondition: if ctx->name does not begin with "none" (strncmp over 4 characters) and no usable elevator type of that name is found by elevator_find_get, it returns -EINVAL before touching the queue. Otherwise (a reference on the found type is held until return) it quiesces the queue; if q->elevator existed, it records it in ctx->old and calls elevator_exit(q). If a new type was found it calls blk_mq_init_sched(q, new_e, &ctx->res): on success q->elevator is the new elevator and ctx->new is set to it; on failure (non-zero return) the old elevator has already been exited, ctx->new is not set, the queue is left with no elevator from this call, and a warning that the switch to the named scheduler failed and falls back to "none" is logged. If no new type was requested ("none") the QUEUE_FLAG_SQ_SCHED flag is cleared, q->elevator = NULL and q->nr_requests = q->tag_set->queue_depth. After a successful switch a blktrace message is added. On every path past the lookup the queue is unquiesced and the reference taken by elevator_find_get is dropped with elevator_put. It returns 0 on success or the error from blk_mq_init_sched.

name: elevator_set_default
prose: Precondition: q is a valid blk-mq request queue with valid q->tag_set, set up before use by the caller. Postcondition: returns nothing. It always clears QUEUE_FLAG_NO_ELV_SWITCH on q. If q->tag_set->flags has BLK_MQ_F_NO_SCHED_BY_DEFAULT it then returns. Otherwise it looks up the "mq-deadline" elevator type with elevator_find_get; if not registered it returns. If found and (q->nr_hw_queues == 1 or the tag set uses shared tags) it calls elevator_change(q, ctx) with no_uevent set to switch to mq-deadline; a negative result is reported with a warning that initialisation failed and falls back to "none" (no scheduler is installed by this call). If the queue has several hardware queues and no shared tags, no switch is attempted. The type reference from elevator_find_get is dropped with elevator_put on every path after a successful lookup.

name: ioprio_check_cap
prose: Precondition: none; ioprio may be any int, read as class = (ioprio >> 13) & 7 and level = ioprio & 0x1fff. Postcondition: returns 0 if class is IOPRIO_CLASS_BE (2) or IOPRIO_CLASS_IDLE (3); returns 0 if class is IOPRIO_CLASS_NONE (0) and level == 0, and -EINVAL if class is NONE and level != 0; for IOPRIO_CLASS_RT (1) returns 0 if the calling task has CAP_SYS_ADMIN or CAP_SYS_NICE, and -EPERM if it has neither; returns -EINVAL for every other class value (4, 5, 6 and IOPRIO_CLASS_INVALID 7). Reads the task capabilities only; no locks, references or memory are acquired or released.
note: No formal contract: the RT case depends on the task capabilities, not on the argument alone.

Postcondition: it first calls ioprio_check_cap(ioprio) and returns its non-zero result (-EPERM or -EINVAL) without further action. Otherwise it takes rcu_read_lock (released before return) with the result initialised to -ESRCH and dispatches on which: for IOPRIO_WHO_PROCESS it uses current if who == 0 else the task found by find_task_by_vpid(who), and if a task is found the result is set_task_ioprio(p, ioprio) (0 or its error); for IOPRIO_WHO_PGRP it iterates under tasklist_lock read lock over every thread of the process group (the caller group if who == 0, else find_vpid(who)), calling set_task_ioprio on each and stopping at the first non-zero result and returning it, giving 0 if all succeeded and -ESRCH if the group has no thread; for IOPRIO_WHO_USER it converts who with make_kuid in the caller user namespace (an invalid uid, or no user found, leaves -ESRCH), then calls set_task_ioprio on every thread whose uid equals that uid and that has a vnr pid, stopping at the first error and returning it, giving 0 if all succeeded and -ESRCH if none matched; when who != 0 the user reference taken by find_user is dropped with free_uid on every path; for any other which the result is -EINVAL.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE2(ioprio_get, int, which, int, who)
prose: Generated syscall ioprio_get(which, who). Precondition: runs in process context; which and who come from user space and may be any ints. Postcondition: takes rcu_read_lock (released before return) with result initialised to -ESRCH and dispatches on which. IOPRIO_WHO_PROCESS: uses current if who == 0, else the task found by find_task_by_vpid(who); if found, the result is get_task_raw_ioprio(p): the security_task_getioprio error if non-zero, else the raw p->io_context->ioprio, or IOPRIO_DEFAULT if the task has no io_context. IOPRIO_WHO_PGRP: iterates under the tasklist_lock read lock over the threads of the process group (caller group if who == 0, else find_vpid(who)); for each, get_task_ioprio(p) (security hook error, else the effective priority) is obtained, tasks with a negative value are skipped, and the result is the numerically smallest (best) value among the rest, or -ESRCH if there is none. IOPRIO_WHO_USER: with uid = make_kuid(current_user_ns(), who), uses current_user() if who == 0 else find_user(uid); if no user is found the result stays -ESRCH, otherwise the result is the best (smallest) get_task_ioprio value over all threads whose uid equals the user uid and that have a vnr pid, skipping negative values, or -ESRCH if none; the user reference from find_user is dropped with free_uid when who != 0. name: adfspart_check_EESOX
prose: Real function is adfspart_check_EESOX(state) (the earlier name eesox_partition does not exist in the source). Precondition: state is a valid struct parsed_partitions with writable pp_buf and a valid state->disk; the function may sleep (it reads a device sector). Postcondition: it reads sector 7 with read_part_sector; if that fails it returns -1 and registers nothing. Otherwise it copies the 256 bytes with each byte XORed with eesox_name[i & 15] into a local buffer, releases the sector with put_dev_sector, and scans up to 8 consecutive 32-byte entries from the start of the buffer, stopping at the first entry whose 6-byte magic differs from "Eesox\0"; let n be the number of consecutive valid entries from index 0 (0 to 8). For each valid entry i >= 1 it calls put_partition(state, slot, start of entry i-1, start of entry i - start of entry i-1) with slots numbered from 1. If n == 0 it registers no partition, does not touch pp_buf and returns 0. If n >= 1 it additionally registers a final partition from the start of entry n-1 to the end of the disk (get_capacity(state->disk) - start), appends a newline to state->pp_buf with strlcat, and returns 1. The sector reference is released on every path; no other references or memory are held.
